findings.quote: whereas someone already occupied with a royal court, if chance and opportunity offered, might perhaps shift to the greater and more illustrious name of Greece.
findings.problem: Greek: οὐδὲ γὰρ προκαταληφθεὶς ὑπὸ βασιλικῆς δυναστείας, καὶ τυχὼν ἐξουσίας, οὐδεὶς ἂν ἐπέσχε σὺν καιρῷ ποιήσασθαι μετάβασιν ἐπὶ τὸ τῆς Ἑλλάδος ὄνομα καὶ πρόσωπον. This is a negated universal (οὐδὲ ... οὐδεὶς ἂν ἐπέσχε: no one, once held by royal power and given the chance, would hold back from the timely change to the name and face of Greece), not a mere possibility ('might perhaps shift'). The English also drops the qualifier ἀκεραίῳ χρώμενος γνώμῃ (with a sound mind) from the preceding clause.
findings.proposed_fix: whereas no one already held by royal power, given the opportunity, would hold back from making the timely change to the name and face of Greece.

units.note: Also uncertain, no fix offered: ἐπικλήτου in 'ἀλόγου καὶ ἐπικλήτου λοιδορίας' is rendered 'borrowed'; the sense of ἐπίκλητος here (reproachable? called in?) is doubtful and 'borrowed' is not well supported, but I cannot establish a better rendering with certainty.
Greek begins mid-sentence with Philip as implied subject; English supplies it correctly.

English omits the source citations (Polybius, book 8) and the grammatical note οὐδετέρως (Hyscana is neuter) from the Stephanus entries; these are apparatus matters, not errors in the translated sense.

findings.quote: a place not open to siege-works but held secure by the continuous presence of Cambylus
findings.problem: Greek: τι τῶν φυλακτηρίων τῶν κατὰ τοὺς ὄπισθε τόπους τῆς ἄκρας, οἵτινες κατασκευὴν μὲν οὐκ ἐπεδέχοντο, τῇ δὲ συνεχείᾳ τῶν ὑπὸ τὸν Καμβύλον τεταγμένων ἀνδρῶν ἐτηροῦντο. κατασκευή is construction or fortification of the posts themselves: these posts did not admit of fortification (the ground did not allow it), and were instead kept secure by the constant presence of Cambylus' men. 'Siege-works' (works by an attacker) misreads the sense.
findings.proposed_fix: which did not admit of fortification but were guarded by the continuous presence of Cambylus

units.note: The fix is written to follow 'one of the guard-posts on the rear side of the citadel, ' directly; the remaining text 'men.' is unchanged.
